title: Console Starter Set: Deprioritization & Feature-Gating Plan for Dashboards, Tracing, and Cost Insights
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Context: We need a clearly bounded first-surface for Redwood Console that shows value to customers while meeting telemetry, latency, and storage constraints for the initial launch. This ticket captures a deliberate deprioritization + feature-gating plan (the "Starter Set") across three verticals: dashboards (insights cards), distributed tracing (service spans UI), and route-level cost breakdowns. Goal: reduce implementation surface by ~60% relative to the full spec while preserving investigative value for customers and enabling a fast, reliable rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: initial product surface limited to four configurable insight tiles: overall traffic QPS, 95th latency, error rate (5xx), and per-route request volume. Each tile has a single timeseries and a 7d baseline comparison. No custom charts, no cohort filters, no data export in v1.

Tracing: show a call-graph flyout for a sampled request with flamegraph summary and a link to raw trace logs. Trace storage capped to 72 hours for the GA tenant; UI surface excludes span-level stats aggregation and no waterfall swimlane for multi-service traces in v1.
Cost breakdown: present route-level aggregated spend (USD) and token counts per route for last 7 days. No per-token breakdown by model variant, no cost forecast, and no per-customer allocation in v1.
Performance: dashboard tile load must render within 800ms on median for demo dataset; trace preview must render within 1.2s for sampled trace payloads under 200KB.
Fallbacks: when time-series data is unavailable, tiles render a clearly labeled placeholder with guidance to retry; no broken UI or silent failures allowed.

Rollout gating: feature toggles implemented so we can enable/disable each starter tile and tracing preview independently; prod rollout requires a canary cohort of internal users and a post-canary health check for 48 hours with no critical errors and acceptable latency targets.
decisions: Cut complex drilldowns: full charting and ad-hoc filtering capabilities deferred to post-GA (Q3). Rationale: reduces backend query surface and SLO risk.
Simplify tracing: store raw spans for only sampled traces and skip building span aggregation indices for v1 to avoid heavy write amplification.
Flatten cost model: present only aggregate route-level metrics rather than per-model or per-deployment at launch to reduce compute and UI complexity.
Feature gates: implement three independent toggles: dashboards-starter, tracing-preview, cost-aggregate to allow progressive exposure and rapid rollback.
Telemetry sampling: default to 0.5% sampling for traces in hosted demo tenants, configurable by enterprise customers in Dedicated/Dedicated+Private plans.
tradeoffs: User empowerment vs velocity: reducing interactive querying removes power users' ability to deep-dive at GA, but enables shipping observable primitives faster and with higher reliability.

Storage cost vs debugging fidelity: short trace retention reduces cost but may hamper investigations that cross the 72-hour boundary; mitigated with explicit guidance to customers and offer extended retention as an enterprise add-on.
Simplicity vs future extensibility: flattening cost breakdown simplifies rollout but will require a migration path for richer attribution data later.
notes: Stakeholders: Product (Ava), Eng (Samir), Design (Leah O'Connor), SRE (Marcus Chen), Sales lead (Priya Rao) — alignment meeting 2026-03-09 produced the starter-set constraints below.
Implementation pattern: backend will expose a single consolidated 'starter' endpoint that returns the four dashboard cards in one request to avoid repeated small queries and reduce cold-start QPS.
Design: tiles must be usable on mobile with reduced density; tracing preview is intentionally modal to avoid expensive background fetches.
Operational: SRE requires circuit-breaker around starter endpoint and a per-tenant rate cap to prevent noisy tenants from impacting latency SLOs.
